clue.text: Traitor shot by CO, a leader of troops

parts.note: to have a shot at something is to have a turn
taken as written: the abbreviation for commanding officer
taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a group is the one at the front, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: first letter of troops

explanation.surface: A deserter is executed by firing squad on the orders of the commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as an execution, but it means a go or a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat is someone who switches sides, which is exactly what a traitor does.

clue.text: One seeking damages losing simple argument

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so the word for simple is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: a plaintiff sues in a civil court, often for compensation
simple and plain are synonyms

explanation.surface: A claimant in a lawsuit drops a straightforward case.
explanation.walkthrough: Take PLAIN off the front of PLAINTIFF to leave TIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a minor quarrel, a small petty argument between people.

clue.text: Rustic artist interrupting canon, endlessly

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so the artist sits inside
without an end means the final letter of the word for canon is cut off

parts.note: a canon is a rule or principle
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter breaks in on a never-ending church law or a never-ending piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canon' suggests church law or a round in music; here it is just a rule. RA, Royal Academician, is the standard crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic and rural are synonyms, both describing the countryside and country life.

clue.text: About to drink gin or cobblers

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
to lap is to drink as a cat does
a gin is a snare or trap for animals

explanation.surface: Someone is about to have a glass of gin, or perhaps some cobblers, a fruit dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' is not the spirit but a trap; 'cobblers' is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious nonsense, which is what the British slang 'cobblers' also means.

clue.text: Guys during a test drive damaged trailer

indicators.note: what happens during something falls within it, so one piece sits inside the other
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
guys are men

explanation.surface: Some men take a car out for a test drive and damage the trailer behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailer' looks like something towed, but it is a film trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: A film trailer is a short advertisement promoting a forthcoming movie.

clue.text: Team audibly expressed relief

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word for the sound of relief is spelt differently from how it sounds

parts.note: a sigh expresses relief; sighed sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: The players breathed out loudly with relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team in a sports match, as in 'the home side'.

clue.text: Screen cast, about 50

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the number

parts.note: to shy is to throw, so cast is shied
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A film screening has a cast of about fifty actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' and 'cast' suggest cinema, but cast means thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: To shield something is to screen it, protecting it from view or harm.

clue.text: Cleaner put off by toff

parts.note: to deter is to put someone off
a toff is a posh gentleman, a gent

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady is put off by an upper-class snob.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for a rich, upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleaning agent, such as washing-up liquid or laundry powder.

clue.text: Finding Italian composer inside ceremonial court

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the composer sits between the other two words

parts.note: ceremonial occasions are formal
CT is the abbreviation for court
Giuseppe Verdi, composer of Aida

explanation.surface: A famous Italian composer is discovered at a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finding' looks like discovering something, but it is a jury's decision.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal verdict is the official finding a jury or judge delivers at the end of a trial.

clue.text: Degrade sister, unwisely, in family magazine

indicators.note: acting unwisely suggests confused, muddled behaviour, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly belittles their sister in a magazine read by the whole family.
explanation.definitionFit: Reader's Digest is a long-running general-interest monthly magazine aimed at a family readership.

clue.text: Put right about couple

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: Fixing things concerning a married couple, perhaps after a row.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair something is to mend it or fix it, so a repaired thing has been put right.

clue.text: Following behind leader in rally

parts.note: behind schedule means late

indicators.note: the leader is at the front, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: first letter of rally

explanation.surface: A driver trails the frontrunner in a motor rally.
explanation.definitionFit: Later and following both mean coming afterwards in time, as in 'the following day'.

clue.text: Generally free

definitions.meaning: second meaning: not captured, as an escaped criminal

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like the phrase 'generally free', but each is a separate meaning of the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'in general, as a whole' and 'at liberty, still uncaptured'.

clue.text: Sailor man, bruiser at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused or lost, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tough brawler of a sailor out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A submariner is a sailor serving in a submarine.

clue.text: Planet could show a change of direction behind sun

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the later pieces follow the letter for sun

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday
taken as written
a turn is a change of direction

explanation.surface: A planet's orbit might swing round behind the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is the sixth planet from the sun, famous for its rings.

clue.text: Attractive blue Fiat crashed outside university

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap around the abbreviation
a crashed car is wrecked and reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A smart blue Fiat car has crashed outside a university campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Beautiful and attractive are synonyms, both meaning pleasing to look at.

clue.text: Fine Greek character making cheese there

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A splendid Greek fellow making cheese in his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' refers back to Greece: the definition is a Greek cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly white cheese made in Greece from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: A critical time for one to leave alluring woman with nothing on

indicators.note: in a down answer, one thing on another is placed above it, so the word for nothing comes first

parts.note: zero is nothing

indicators.note: to leave is to go away, so the letter for one is taken out

parts.note: a houri is a beautiful nymph of Islamic paradise, hence an alluring woman
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A seductive woman wearing nothing at a critical moment, prompting someone to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: A houri is one of the beautiful maidens of the Islamic paradise. In a down entry, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero hour is the moment an operation is scheduled to begin, a critical time.

clue.text: Adult feeding toddler perfectly

indicators.note: feeding something puts it inside, so the adult letter goes into the child

parts.note: a tot is a small child
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up spoon-feeds a small child with perfect care.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'to a T' means exactly or perfectly, as in 'it suits you to a T'.

clue.text: Young landlord brought round second bulletin

indicators.note: brought round means placed around, so the outer words enclose the abbreviation

parts.note: young and new are synonyms
a landlord lets property, so is a letter
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A young landlord, revived after fainting, issues another notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landlord' gives LETTER, one who lets, not a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsletter is a regular bulletin of news sent to members or subscribers.

clue.text: Eminent female, a mostly shy person

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for shy person is dropped

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
taken as written
a timid, retiring person is called a mouse

explanation.surface: A distinguished woman who is mostly rather shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous and eminent are near-synonyms, both meaning widely known and respected.

clue.text: Struggle to survive in desert heat

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray
a heat is a preliminary race

explanation.surface: Fighting for life in the scorching heat of the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' and 'heat' look like sand and sun, but they are a verb and a sporting heat.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the fierce, competitive scramble of working life, a struggle to get by.

clue.text: United aware of final in Rome

parts.note: to be in on a secret is to be aware of it

indicators.note: the final of something is its end, so only the last letter of the city is kept

parts.note: last letter of Rome

explanation.surface: A United team is aware of a cup final being held in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In one means combined or united, as in 'two functions in one'.

clue.text: The Spanish embarrassed over senior church member

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means turned upwards, so the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: red-faced with embarrassment

explanation.surface: A Spanish churchman is red-faced in front of a senior colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a senior lay official in some churches, such as Presbyterian ones.

clue.text: Show yellow card to reserve

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a football referee ... a player by showing a yellow card

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests cautioning a substitute player; 'reserve' is instead a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both a referee cautioning a footballer and making an advance reservation.

clue.text: How Monopoly starts, as it always has

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: every player begins on the square marked GO
second meaning: right from the very beginning

explanation.walkthrough: In the board game Monopoly, play begins on the corner square labelled GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means from the very outset, so something that has been true since then has always been so.

clue.text: Additional matter involving learner driver

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the learner letter is wrapped inside

parts.note: pus is the matter that oozes from an infected wound
L-plates mark a learner driver

explanation.surface: An extra issue concerning someone learning to drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matter' is not an issue but the yellowish fluid in a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus as an adjective means extra or additional, as in 'a plus factor'.

clue.text: Kirk series open about closure of kirk?

parts.note: to open is to start
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its end, so only its last letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of the lower-case kirk at the end of the clue

explanation.surface: A series of sermons begins about a Scottish church closing down.
explanation.walkthrough: A kirk is a Scottish church; Captain Kirk commands the starship Enterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Trek is the science-fiction TV series whose most famous captain is James T Kirk.
